source: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 14 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 14
lead: Choose a condition on p that is necessary but not sufficient for the equation to have exactly one real root.
knowledgePattern: Find the cubic root-count range before classifying a weaker condition
solution:
Use the clarified direction stated above the source question: choose a condition on p which is necessary but not sufficient for the equation to have exactly one real root. This is the direction used by the publisher’s worked answer.

Let f(x)=2x3−3px2+p. Then f′(x)=6x(x−p). For p ≠ 0 the two turning inputs are 0 and p, with heights p and p−p3.

A positive-leading cubic has exactly one real root when these two turning heights have the same strict sign. Their product is p2(1−p2), so this requires 0<|p|<1. If p = 0 the equation is 2x3=0, also giving exactly one real root.

At p = ±1 a turning height is zero: the graph touches the axis at one input and crosses at another, giving two distinct real roots. For |p| > 1 it has three. Therefore the exact one-root range is −1<p<1.

Option B, −1 ≤ p ≤ 1, contains every successful p but also p = 1, which fails. It is necessary but not sufficient. A is equivalent, C and D omit successful values, and E and F each omit one side of the successful interval. Answer B.

hints.title: Find where the cubic turns
hints.body: Differentiate with respect to x, treating p as a constant. Factor the derivative to find the stationary inputs.
hints.recap: Derivative zeros split a graph into pieces where it rises or falls.
hints.pitfall: Check separately when the two stationary inputs coincide.
hints.pause: Find the stationary inputs and substitute them into the original cubic.

recall.reminder: Derivative zeros split a graph into pieces where it rises or falls.

hints.title: Use the two heights to count roots
hints.body: Sketch the cubic when both turning heights are above the axis, when both are below, and when they lie on opposite sides.
hints.recap: Use turning-point heights to count where a graph meets the horizontal axis.
hints.pitfall: A touching root and a crossing root at different inputs count as two distinct roots.
hints.pause: Find the exact range of p giving one real root, including the cases with a zero turning height.

recall.reminder: Use turning-point heights to count where a graph meets the horizontal axis.

hints.title: Apply the direction stated above the question
hints.body: You need a condition on p that includes every successful value but also includes at least one value that fails.
hints.recap: Necessary means the condition holds whenever the target holds; not sufficient means it also permits a failure.
hints.pitfall: An exact match to your successful interval would be sufficient as well as necessary.
hints.pause: Compare the whole interval and its endpoints with each option.
